roller.contact: rubber tyre dia 8 on the cage outside (r 21.5), z 62 to 78, now free with the inner ring gone

options.name: Slide in the free band under the root + a rocker on each root
options.how: A static blade slides in radially at the station, under the finger and above the bead. It pushes the two rocker tips of the root standing there: the rocker pulls both pins 0.5 mm in and 2.1 mm up, and the blade's notch holds the root and its bead while the roller turns the hub.
options.rotor: 4 rockers on the roots, est. 0.4 g each
options.static: SG92R servo on the slide (25 N at a 10 mm horn vs 8 N needed), N20 roller on the cage, QTR-1A
options.access: free band z 86.0 to 89.7 (3.7 mm) from r 26.9 outward, under the finger, above the ring flange
options.risk: new rocker in a crowded root block

options.name: Prongs rise from below through slots in the ring flange
options.how: Two prongs climb at r 27.5 through slots in the spinning flange (lined up when parked), ramp the tabs inward, lift them and hold the root.
options.rotor: 24 to 36 slots in the pull-ring flange
options.static: SG92R on a vertical slide, N20 roller, QTR-1A
options.access: free column at the station from z 60 to the tabs (yokes, idlers, cords all elsewhere)
options.risk: flange bending at stall 43.8 MPa now, 87.5 MPa with slots (PA-CF)

options.name: Contacts touch the parked root; shape-memory wire lifts the pins
options.how: Pogo pins on the static side touch two pads on the root at the station; a Flexinol / Muscle Wire loop in the root block pulls the pins in and up. Hold by a fork on the bead.
options.rotor: 4 x 0.005 in wires per root (2.2 N each at 200 mA), pads, est. 0.6 g per root
options.static: pogo block + fork servo, N20 roller, QTR-1A
options.access: pads must sit in the same band as A's rocker tips
options.risk: needs the same access as A plus wiring on every root; wire fatigue

options.name: Another Cephalo hand moves the roots
options.how: A neighbouring arm's hand grips the root, presses the tabs and turns it; the rotor is held by its own pins on the other roots.
options.access: from outside, at the tabs and fingers
options.risk: needs a second hand within reach and fine control; slow

options.name: Set the roots by hand between flights
options.how: The user lifts the two tabs with a fingernail and slides the root; the pose is fixed for the next flight.
options.risk: no pose change during a mission

options.name: Flight motor turns the hub, static fork holds the root
options.how: The ESC creeps the rotor round while a fork holds the lifted root.
options.static: fork + lifter (same access problem as A)
options.risk: sensorless ESC cannot creep 30 deg reliably at standstill
